_note:
P4's single-turn finding, applied to the five remaining PREREQUISITE-CARD tools. The ONLY changed fields are `approve` and `max_approvals`; prompts, seeds and falsifiers are carried over UNEDITED, because a re-run must measure the same request the original conclusion was drawn from.

Proven on kg_propose_edge first: it read called 0/5 for the whole loop because every scenario was approve=None and single-turn, so the turn ended at the PREREQUISITE's card and the tool was unreachable by construction. With the card approved it went 0/5 -> 5/5 called and 5/5 landed, and is now proven through every gate bar.

WHAT WOULD REFUTE THIS: a tool still called 0/5 with its prerequisite approved. Then its block is NOT the approval gate and the P4 reading is wrong for that tool — recorded per tool, not explained away.

scenarios.prompt: Override entity field — in this book Aldric Vane should be a cartographer, not a soldier.
scenarios.prompt_source: meta.synonyms['override entity field'] + ['add entity override'], verbatim, plus the entity's name so the target is unambiguous.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: The entity must exist — the tool takes a target_entity_id and the model has to resolve the NAME to it, which is the step that has failed repeatedly in this loop.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM entity_override WHERE project_id='{project_id}'
seed_assert.why: ZERO overrides before, so any override is attributable to this turn — and, the card never being approved, the count must still be 0 afterwards.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: an override lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model invents a target_entity_id rather than resolving 'Aldric Vane', OR the op chosen is not `add` when the entity has no override yet — its enum spans add|update|delete|restore, and `delete` on a request to ADD a field change would be the worst outcome. Store check: entity_override stays 0.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a target_entity_id or override_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — deleting an already-deleted override must refuse, not report a second success. Checked deliberately: that is the exact shape of the arc_template archive defect found in batch 15.

scenarios.prompt: Build the knowledge graph for this book — extract the cast from my story.
scenarios.prompt_source: meta.synonyms['build the knowledge graph'] + ['extract the cast from my story'], verbatim.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: ZERO entities before. This tool runs a WHOLE PIPELINE (plan a worklist, build it, project a knowledge graph) and spends on every stage, so the card is never approved and the glossary must be untouched afterwards.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: entities are created with NO confirm card, OR the op chosen is not `start` on a first request — its enum spans start|approve_plan|status|project_kg|approve_edges|cancel, and `approve_plan` or `approve_edges` would be approving a plan the author has never seen, which is the worst outcome for a tool whose whole design is a human checkpoint between stages — OR the model invents a run_id for a run that has not started. CONTROL: a fresh book has no story text beyond one seeded chapter, so a build with nothing to extract from is itself worth seeing.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A, multi-stage, and it spends at every stage.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — op=status/approve_plan with a run_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — op=start twice must not launch two runs for the same book.

scenarios.prompt: Aldric Vane appears in this chapter — mark where he shows up.
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['this character appears in this chapter'] + ['mark where this character shows up'].

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: The entity must exist; the tool takes an entity_id and the model has to resolve the NAME to it.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM chapter_entity_links WHERE entity_id IN (SELECT entity_id FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}')
seed_assert.why: ZERO links before, so any link is attributable to this turn — and, since the card is never approved, the count must still be 0 afterwards.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the link lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model invents an entity_id or chapter_id rather than resolving them, OR it links to a chapter that is not the one open in the editor. The store check is glossary_chapter_links: unchanged, because the card is never approved.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — an entity_id or chapter_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — its description says it ERRORS if the entity is already linked to that chapter; that refusal is the audit.

scenarios.prompt: Back up Aldric Vane's role with a passage from the chapter — cite where it says he climbed the black stair.
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['back this up with a passage'] + ['cite where this is stated'].

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: The entity must exist. NOTE the deeper precondition this scenario is really testing: evidence attaches to an ATTRIBUTE VALUE (attr_value_id), not to the entity, so the model must first find or create an attribute value. If it cannot, that is a PRECONDITION-CHAIN finding like kg_propose_edge's, not a defect in this tool.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: evidence lands with NO confirm card, OR the quoted original_text is not actually in the chapter (a fabricated citation is the worst outcome here), OR the model invents an attr_value_id. CONTROL: the fixture has no attribute values, so a turn that cannot proceed is the precondition chain, and that must be recorded as such rather than as a tool failure.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — an attr_value_id that does not exist must be refused.

scenarios.prompt: Create the chapters — make the plan real for this book.
scenarios.prompt_source: meta.synonyms['create the chapters'] + ['make the plan real'], verbatim.

args.source_markdown:
# Emberfall

## Arc I — The Emberfall
### Chapter 1 — The Ember Codex
Aldric Vane climbs the black stair.
### Chapter 2 — The Waterline
The Obsidian Trench is walkable only at low tide.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM chapters WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: ONE chapter — the fixture's own — before anything is applied. This tool CREATES real book chapters from a previewed proposal, so the count moving is the whole signal. The card is never approved, so it must still be 1 afterwards. CONTROL: `proposal_id` comes from plan_bootstrap_propose, which has NOT been run here, so the honest outcome may be a refusal naming the missing proposal — a PRECONDITION finding rather than a tool defect.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: chapters are created with NO confirm card (Tier A — this materialises real book content), OR the model invents a proposal_id, OR the reply claims chapters were created while the card is still pending. Store check: loreweave_book.chapters stays at 1.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A, and it creates real chapters.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a proposal_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — applying the same proposal twice must not create the chapters twice.
